govdocs-archive_org-nsia-HooversNotesKin: Martin Waldron’s Several Books Planned on Ray Case is a New York Times piece. The Ray case drew authors fast. Publishers smelled money. The books came quickly. The file belongs to the press archive. The item is a fragment of press history.
the-lives-of-the-twelve-caesars-volume-0: In the chaos of 69 AD — the Year of the Four Emperors — Marcus Otho seized the throne and held it for barely three months. Suetonius paints him as vain and extravagant, yet capable of a noble end: rather than prolong civil war, he took his own life after a single lost battle. A brief, tragic life from Rome's most turbulent year.
the-history-of-the-reign-of-ferdinand-an: Prescott's third volume completes his history of Ferdinand and Isabella — the consolidation of Spain, the Italian wars, and the monarchs' final years. A monumental close to a monumental work. The book that made American history-writing world-famous. It remains the classic English account of Spain's most glorious age.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-ayacucho: A 1913 entry on Ayacucho — the Peruvian archdiocese of the highlands. The entry tells its Andean story. Its churches guard the colonial art. The Quechua faithful fill its pews. A highland see of the south. Its Holy Week fills the streets.
